step_3_nearest_governing_principle_in_th.quote_2: docs/math-foundations.md, Section 5, audit conclusion: 'The approximations found are all **documented in code** (burn GCD estimate, BC stack constant, Terminus pen average, R single-cast, DoT even-split, stat rounding, prefix double-on-hit attribution) - none is silently presented as exact.'
step_3_nearest_governing_principle_in_th.quote_3: docs/math-foundations.md, Section 0: 'The validity of replacing `E[f(X)]` by `f(E[X])` is the one place the engine is genuinely approximate: it is exact for affine `f` (linearity of expectation) and biased for strictly convex/concave `f` (Jensen). Every family below is labeled accordingly.'
derivation: Section 5 IS, structurally, a disposition map: it is a table whose rows are engine families (identified by their code locations, i.e. by where their outputs live) and whose verdict column carries exactly one of EXACT / EXACT* / APPROX.
Section 0 states the labelling obligation is per-family and exhaustive ('Every family below is labeled accordingly').

The Section 5 legend and audit conclusion make the obligation normative and directional: an APPROX quantity must NEVER be presented as exact. A presentation surface that carries no disposition at all presents every quantity as unqualified - which is the failure mode the doc explicitly forbids.

Therefore a per-leaf {disposition, view_tag} map attached to a combat result is the machine-readable instantiation of the Section 5 discipline, and a combat result carrying NO such map is the state the doc argues against.

This yields a directional verdict on presence/absence. It does NOT yield the map's contents: the doc's dispositions are assigned per engine family, and mapping engine families onto this scenario's specific leaf paths requires reading src/, which the runbook forbids.

Whether the disposition assigned to any given leaf is the right one (e.g. whether a leaf fed by `_add_burn_damage` is correctly marked APPROX rather than EXACT). Section 5 fixes the per-family verdicts, but binding families to this scenario's leaf paths requires src/, which is out of bounds.
The controlled vocabulary of `view_tag` - it appears nowhere in the permitted evidence.

independent_computation.confidence: LOW-MODERATE, and directional only. The verdict below is a judgement on presence-vs-absence, not an element-wise validation of the map.

verdict_rationale: The leaf is metadata, so the cached wiki corpus cannot adjudicate it - and it does not contradict the corpus either (0 hits, no conflict surface). The only governing principle available in permitted evidence is the labelling discipline of math-foundations Sections 0 and 5, which requires that every engine family carry a disposition and that an approximation is 'never silently presented as exact'. A combat result with NO dispositions map is precisely the unlabelled state that discipline forbids; a result carrying a per-leaf {disposition, view_tag} map is its machine-readable form. So the old <absent> state is the weaker one on the only axis I can evaluate, and 'both_wrong' would assert a defect I have no evidence for. Registered with an explicit caveat: this endorses the PRESENCE and SHAPE of the map, not its contents, which were never supplied to me and which cannot be checked without reading src/.
caveats: Not an element-wise validation. If the audit question is whether specific leaves got the right disposition, this receipt does not answer it and a src-reading reviewer must.
The new value was described to me only by schema, never by data. A concrete map would be needed to raise confidence above LOW-MODERATE.
No combat-number leaf is touched by this change, so no numeric regression follows from it either way.
